title: Missing Secondary Group Memberships in SSSD with Active Directory | SUSE | Support Center
plain_text:
Missing Secondary Group Memberships in SSSD with Active Directory
Environment
Help Environment

SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 12

Situation

An Active Directory (AD) user is a member of multiple security groups, but the id command on a Linux client shows an incomplete list of groups. This occurs even when the gidNumber attribute is correctly replicated to the Global Catalog (GC). The environment typically uses:

ID Provider: SSSD with id_provider = ad or id_provider = ldap.

ID Mapping: Manual POSIX attributes are enforced (ldap_id_mapping = False).

Attributes: gidNumber is present on both the LDAP (389) and GC (3268) ports.

Problem

When ldap_use_tokengroups is enabled (default for the AD provider), SSSD uses the tokenGroups attribute to resolve memberships. This attribute returns a list of SIDs rather than full objects.

In an environment where ldap_id_mapping = False, a race condition or logic conflict occurs:

SSSD retrieves the list of group SIDs via tokenGroups.

Because SSSD is instructed not to map SIDs to IDs automatically, it must then resolve each SID to find its associated gidNumber.

If this resolution occurs via a high-performance SID-to-Name path, the POSIX attributes (gidNumber) may not be evaluated or cached correctly during the initial initgroups request.

The result is a "ghost group" in the cache: SSSD knows the user is a member, but because the GID wasn't linked during the high-speed SID lookup, the group is omitted from the user's identity.

Running getent group <groupname> triggers a full LDAP object lookup (Port 389), which forces SSSD to see the gidNumber and "repair" the cache entry.

Resolution

Disabling tokenGroups forces SSSD to use a standard LDAP memberOf search. This method retrieves the group objects as full LDAP entries from the start, ensuring the gidNumber is read and applied immediately.

1. Modify the SSSD configuration Edit /etc/sssd/sssd.conf and add the following parameter to the [domain/NAME] section:

[domain/your_domain]
...
ldap_use_tokengroups = False
...

 

2. Clear the SSSD Cache To ensure all groups are re-evaluated using the new lookup method, purge the local database:

systemctl stop sssd
rm -f /var/lib/sss/db/*
systemctl start sssd

 

Cause

The tokenGroups mechanism is optimized for Windows-style SID-based authorization. In a Linux environment requiring explicit gidNumber attributes, this optimization can bypass the necessary POSIX attribute retrieval. Switching to ldap_use_tokengroups = False ensures that SSSD performs a search that explicitly fetches the group objects and their attributes, providing consistent group visibility.
